messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: potential cross-tenant read detected in Dedicated pool d-pool-7 (customer: OrionHealth). Metric spike: 5 anomalous kvcache reads flagged by crosscheck. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/3504009876
eng-oncall-marc: Oncall here, looking. Marc — starting incident thread. Can someone pull the routing snapshot + kvcache ownership for d-pool-7?
sre-jen: I have the pool. Suspect path: d-pool-7 -> nat-proxy-3 -> node-58. I'll dump recent prefix table now.
infra-ryan: grabbing routing table + recent route updates from 3504009000 to 3504009876. Also checking if there was any recent config push to proxy-agent in us-east-2.
prod-support-lina: Reached out to OrionEng to confirm customer-visible symptoms. @customer-orion-alex any reports of misrouted responses or stale data?
customer-orion-alex: We saw two reports from our internal QA — snippets of unrelated tenant responses included in generated outputs around 11:12am. Not high volume but reproducible with same prompt. We're paused on production traffic.
sre-jen: That matches the alert window. Evidence so far: kvcache keys with mismatched tenant prefixes observed on node-58. Still collecting logs.
eng-oncall-marc: Triage plan: 1) Isolate d-pool-7 from shared proxies if possible (no restart). 2) Collect heap/KV state, cache keys, and request traces for those keys. 3) Assess scope across other pools. 4) Notify legal/security if PII possible.
security-elaine: Please collect the plaintext of the anomalous outputs and mark them as evidence. If PII, escalate to Sec and Compliance. Do not share residues outside the thread.
infra-ryan: Executing temporary route withdraw to nat-proxy-3 for d-pool-7. Command posted to ops channel and will be in audit.
incident-bot: Action: Route-withdraw job queued (job-id: rw-3504009876). Operator: infra-ryan. ETA effect: ~30s to 2m.
eng-oncall-marc: Good. While that's happening, Jen — can you confirm whether this is kvcache prefix shadowing versus request routing? Quick heuristic: check kvcache keys for tenant ID collisions (strip -> lower).
sre-jen: Running scan: found ~12 keys on node-58 with prefix overlap (tenant suffix mismatch). Sample key output:
```
key: "tenant:orion:session:abc123" -> value starts with "{...customer:lyra...}"
key: "tenant:lyra:session:def456" -> value correct
```
Looks like writes from tenant lyra landed under orion-prefixed keys.
prod-support-lina: That sample is not fully PII but demonstrates cross-tenant cache contamination. Lina to Orion: we will preserve all data, do a forensics export, and avoid copying into external docs.
customer-orion-alex: Please keep us in the loop. Our contract requires notification within 2 hours for cross-tenant exposure.
eng-oncall-marc: Understood. Timeline note added. Jen — how widespread? Are writes coming from a single proxy or multiple?
sre-jen: Trace matches point writes originating from proxy agent id pa-9 (nat-proxy-3). Correlation: there was a config reload at 3504009200 that changed prefix handling logic (de-dupe path). Looking at code push id: cp-2026.
infra-ryan: Confirmed cp-2026 rollout targeted nat-proxy-*. Rollout window overlapped with traffic to d-pool-7. Rolling back cp-2026 on nat-proxy-3 now.
eng-oncall-marc: Rollback in progress — monitor for stop of anomalous writes. Also, start draining offending node-58 for deep inspection. No full restart yet; prefer controlled drain.
incident-bot: Rollback job initiated (job-id: rb-3504009899).
sre-jen: After rollback, observed write pattern stopped within 45s. New scans show zero new cross-prefix writes. Existing contaminated keys remain. Dumped those keys to forensics bucket: s3://forensics/3504009876/orion/keys.txt (access logged).
prod-support-lina: Notifying OrionEng: we have stopped the active contamination, preserving evidence, working on remediation/cleanup options.
customer-orion-alex: Thanks. Requesting list of affected keys and timestamps. We're starting an internal impact assessment.
security-elaine: I'll take triage on PII. Initial analysis: values contain user identifiers in test data. Marking as potential sensitive. We need to follow data incident playbook. Elaine assigned.
infra-ryan: For immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) revoke any kv-cache TTL relaxations, 2) expire contaminated keys by tenant prefix, 3) schedule controlled purges and rehydration from canonical store after Orion sign-off.
eng-oncall-marc: Ops action: expire keys for prefix tenant:orion:session:* with 1h TTL to reduce risk; do not purge immediately until legal ok. Command executed.
sre-jen: Also enabling read-only mode for d-pool-7 for Orion while we coordinate cleanup — prevents further writes but allows reads for diagnostics.
prod-support-lina: Informing Orion of read-only mode. Lina -> Orion: would you like a maintenance window to run your own audits?
customer-orion-alex: Yes please. We'll run replays against our QA keys and can validate once you do the purge/rehydration plan. We need a timeline.
eng-oncall-marc: ETA for cleanup plan doc: 90 minutes. Will include key list, purge schedule, rehydrate steps, and verification checklist. Postmortem owner: marc.
security-elaine: Escalation: Incident classified as Sev 2 (potential customer data exposure). Notify CISO.
incident-bot: Pager update: Sev 2 — stakeholders notified.
prod-support-lina: Customer comms draft queued. Will send initial update (preserving wording for legal review).
infra-ryan: Follow-up: we found that the proxy config reload didn't atomically apply prefix map, causing a race on write path. Patch proposed: add atomic swap + validation on reload. Putting code review link: https://git.internal/redwood/proxy/patches/458.
sre-jen: Can we add an automated post-reload prefix-sanity check to detect this in future? I'll open a ticket.
eng-oncall-marc: Yes please. Also add monitoring rule to fire on any kvcache key with tenant mismatch confidence > 0.7.
customer-orion-alex: Appreciate the fast response. We'll hold off on any external notifications until we review full key list and legal confirms.
prod-support-lina: Noted. I'll coordinate legal review.
ing-eng-marc: assigning follow-ups: [oncall->marc], [forensics->jen], [security->elaine], [infra->ryan], [customer-comm->lina].
eng-oncall-marc: Quick retrospective note: avoid deploying prefix-handling changes during high-traffic windows on nat proxies until safety checks are in place.
security-elaine: After cleanup we need to run a scoped audit across other dedicated pools that used cp-2026 during rollout window (3504009000-3504009900).
sre-jen: Starting cluster-wide scan for similar contamination across pools. Will update.
incident-bot: Thread closed for paging but remains open for coordination. Add reaction :white_check_mark: when you hand off work.
eng-oncall-marc: Thanks all. Marking this thread as primary incident doc for now. We'll create a formal incident report once cleanups and audits complete.
